name: The Great Mosque of Djenné
context: The largest mud-brick building in the world, rebuilt in 1907 on the site of a 13th-century mosque. Every year the whole town replasters its banco walls. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.

archives.title: Djenne Mosque Dubois 1911
archives.description: The Great Mosque of Djenné was built in 1906-1907 on the ruins of an earlier mosque. This view shows the north east corner.

archives.title: Djenne Fortier 407

archives.title: Djenne Fortier 413 - Ruines de l'ancienne Mosquée
archives.description: Collection Générale Fortier, Dakar 413: Ruines de l'ancienne Mosquée A postcard by Edmond Fortier showing the ruins of the ancient mosque in Djenné. The view shows the northeast corner of the mosque with the eastern ( qibla ) wall on the left and the north wall on the right. This card is included on page 157 No 132 in: Gardi, Bernard; Maas, Pierre; Mommersteeg, Geert (1995), Djenné, il y a cent ans, Amsterdam: Institute Royal des Tropiques, ISBN 90-6832-250-8 .

archives.title: Djenne ruins ancient mosque - Albert Rousseau
archives.description: Ruins of the ancient mosque of Djenné. The view shows the northern wall of the mosque with the eastern ( qibla ) wall on the left. The photograph was published in: Hugot, Ludovic (1895). "Notes de voyage d'un officier au Soudan". À travers le monde (in French). Paris: Librairie Hachette. pp. 214–216 .
